subject: Cognitive Science
title: Semantic Networks
description: A short lesson to help you apply Semantic Networks.

hook.text: Say "nurse" and people think of "doctor" almost instantly. Concepts are linked in a mental web.

buildup.text: Collins and Quillian modeled concepts as nodes in a network connected by labeled relations.

discovery.text: "A canary is a bird" is verified faster than "a canary is an animal" because fewer links are crossed.

twist.text: But high-frequency associations break the distance rule. "A dog is an animal" is very fast too.

climax.text: Spreading activation explains it: activating one node sends energy rippling to its neighbors.

punchline.text: Thinking one thought primes the next.

quiz.question: What is spreading activation in semantic networks?
options: Activating one concept primes related concepts

details.summary: Semantic networks model concepts as nodes connected by labeled relationships. Bird is connected to can fly, has feathers, and is an animal. Spreading activation travels along links, so activating bird primes related concepts like nest and wing.
details.whyItMatters: Semantic networks were among the first computational models of meaning. They showed how knowledge can be organized as connected nodes rather than isolated definitions.
takeaways: Concepts are nodes; relationships are links between them
Activation spreads from one concept to related ones
The model explains priming and organized memory retrieval

faq.question: What is spreading activation?
faq.answer: When a concept is activated, energy spreads to connected concepts, making them temporarily easier to access. Hearing doctor makes nurse easier to recognize because they are closely linked. The closer the connection, the stronger and faster the activation spreads through the network.

faq.question: How are semantic networks different from categories?
faq.answer: Categories group items by shared membership. Semantic networks represent all types of relationships, including part-of, causes, and location links. A category is a subset of what a semantic network can represent. Networks capture richer knowledge structures than simple category membership.
